messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Is phyloPCA a pPCA?
parts:
Laura,

What is meant by “phylogenetically corrected”?  Because a phylo-PCA, as introduced by Revell (2009) is not phylogenetically corrected.  Revell was clear about this, indicating PGLS would still need to be performed with phylo-PCA scores in a linear model analysis.  Rather, phylo-PCA merely rotates a data space, preserving variation in a non-transformed data space.  To perform this analysis,

GLS = TRUE, transform = FALSE

If you want to “correct” for phylogeny, much the way a PGLS analysis does, then change to transform = TRUE, but be aware this is not a phylo-PCA, as defined by Revell (2009).  Either way, yes, GLS = TRUE.

Mike
